title: Hybrid Metric Orchestrator for Granular Capacity Fencing and Anticipatory Scaling
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Dedicated fleets must honor per-tenant throughput guarantees while staying within cost and hardware safety envelopes. Existing autoscalers either react to a single signal (e.g., p95 latency) or apply conservative step limits that cause repeated oscillation or unnecessary overprovisioning. We need an autoscaling policy engine that composes multiple target metrics across time horizons, reasons about short-term demand spikes vs persistent load changes, and enforces hard safety fences (thermal/GPU queue depth/credit budgets) and soft cost fences (headroom credits).

Scope: Design and implement a hybrid metric orchestrator inside the autoscaling controller that supports: multi-horizon targets (instantaneous concurrency, 1-min p50 throughput, 10-min p95 latency), predictive short-horizon forecasts for anticipatory scaling, dynamic step-sizing based on observed signal variance, and explicit safety limits including per-fleet headroom budgets and emergency venting rules. This ticket covers spec, simulation harness, controller prototype, integration tests, and a migration plan for existing scaling policies.

Goals:
- Maintain per-tenant throughput guarantees with >99.5% adherence under synthetic and production traces.
- Avoid >3x overshoot versus steady-state capacity across bursty workloads.
- Provide deterministic rollback path when hardware safety limits are approached.
- Expose policy knobs in Console for ops teams to tune headroom, aggressiveness, and cost-fencing parameters.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can ingest multiple metric signals and compute a unified scale intent (desired worker count) given a policy config
Simulations on 12 recorded production traces show median SLA adherence >= 99.5% and 95th percentile cost overhead <= 1.8x baseline for sustained spikes
Controller implements: short-horizon forecast (0-30s), long-horizon averaging (5-15min), variance-aware step scaling, and hard safety fences (thermal, GPU-memory, reserved-headroom) toggles
Console exposes policy fields: primary_metric, secondary_metrics, forecast_horizon, max_step_pct, headroom_budget, emergency_vent_threshold, rollback_window
Integration tests validate emergency venting by simulating a hardware thermal event and confirm rollback to safe capacity within the configured rollback_window
Documentation: design doc and runbook for on-call detailing failure modes, expected alerts, and postmortem steps
implementation_plan: Week 1: Finalize policy DSL and configuration schema; align with PM/Product on Console fields
Week 2: Build simulation harness ingesting historical traces and synthetic spike generators; implement baseline composite metric fuser
Week 3: Implement forecasting module (lightweight exponential smoothing + short-window AR estimator) and variance-aware stepper algorithm
Week 4: Integrate safety fences: headroom budget accounting, emergency venting hook, and per-fleet hard caps; add telemetry emitters for decisions
Week 5: Run large-scale simulations, tune knobs to meet acceptance criteria; add integration tests and canary rollout plan
Week 6: Console integration and feature flags for staged rollout; docs and on-call runbook; begin controlled rollouts to 2 dedicated fleets
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Forecast inaccuracy leads to underprovisioning during very short spikes. Mitigation: keep conservative min_step and a short-term reactive fallback that temporarily prioritizes latency SLOs over cost

Risk: Emergency venting could trigger cascading scale-downs. Mitigation: add explicit per-tenant and per-fleet hysteresis windows and circuit breaker thresholds; require two independent safety signals to trigger full vent

Risk: Increased complexity makes debugging hard for on-call. Mitigation: emit structured decision traces (policy inputs, score contributions, final intent) to the Console trace view and add a decision replay tool in the runbook
Risk: Cost blowout during misconfiguration. Mitigation: default headroom_budget conservatively; require ops approval for high headroom on critical fleets; include budget checks in release gating
notes: This design intentionally separates intent compute from the executor to keep the controller auditable and testable (intent = desired worker count; executor applies placement and allocation)
Prefer lightweight forecasting to avoid heavy ML infra; accuracy targets are modest (short-term 10-30s) and will be evaluated by simulation

Headroom credits are a soft currency tracked per-fleet: credits accrue during underutilized windows and are consumed during bursts; they cap the allowable temporary overshoot relative to committed capacity
Emergency venting hook will integrate with infra safety signals (node thermal alerts, GPU ECC errors, queue depth). We will standardize signal format with infra team (see ENG-160123 for related work)
